trust_decision.summary: Whether flag bits in a peer-supplied PFCP IE may drive fixed-size field reads beyond the IE's own wire length (octet->len); decided in the per-IE parsers in lib/pfcp/types.c, whose callers only compare the returned size with the IE length after the reads have already happened.

landing_point.why: The summary names the Dropped DL Traffic Threshold IE; ogs_pfcp_parse_dropped_dl_traffic_threshold reads flags and two 8-byte fields with no length check.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All published sites are sibling parser functions in one file (lib/pfcp/types.c:156-635); the closest thing to an off-path site is ogs_pfcp_parse_volume_measurement (lib/pfcp/types.c:581), reached only from the SMF in the UPF-to-SMF direction (src/smf/n4-handler.c:1548, src/smf/n4-handler.c:1744), which is a direction variant rather than a separate module.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The uncovered reads are not 'IE parsers' at all but direct struct casts of IE data in node-specific handlers (src/smf, src/upf, src/sgwu, src/sgwc), and the peer sending them (UPF to SMF, SMF to UPF) is an operator-controlled N4/Sxa node, so a solver can argue they are a different IE, a different layer and a trusted interface.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: IEs that legitimately carry only some optional fields must still decode, e.g. a Volume/Dropped-DL threshold with only one flag set (length 1+8), and an SMF Usage Report with no Volume Measurement (time/event URR): with presence 0 and length 0 the SMF still calls the parser and must keep accumulating duration and the report trigger. An over-broad fix that turns a zero-length or flags-only IE into a hard error makes the caller `continue` and silently drops Gy duration/trigger accounting.

O6_input_shapes: zero-length IE (flags octet itself out of range) in volume, dropped-DL threshold and volume-measurement parsers
flags-only IE with one or more flag bits set but the 8-byte fields absent
IE truncated partway through a later optional field (each of tovol/ulvol/dlvol/tonop/ulnop/dlnop, dlpa/dlby)
SDF Filter with FD set and a flow_description_len larger than the remaining IE bytes

O7_producer.where: lib/core/ogs-tlv-msg.c:572-578 (generic TLV decoder sets octet data/len for OGS_TLV_VAR_STR IEs with no per-IE minimum length; descriptors e.g. lib/pfcp/message.c:557-565 declare VAR_STR)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SMF Session Report Request: Downlink Data Service Information IE cast to a 2-byte struct and its flag-selected byte read with no IE length check, in the same handler as the fixed Volume Measurement route
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: different IE in a downlink-data branch, struct is only 2 bytes, and the sender is the operator's own UPF
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: src/smf vs lib/pfcp/types.c: other file, other package

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SMF Session Report Request: Error Indication Report's Remote F-TEID cast to ogs_pfcp_f_teid_t and teid/IPv4/IPv6 fields read according to flag bits with no IE length check
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: an 'F-TEID lookup' helper in context.c, not a parser, and only an error-indication path
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: lib/pfcp/context.c, same package, different file; reached from src/smf/n4-handler.c:1722

O8_uncovered_routes.route: UPF Session Establishment Request: CP F-SEID cast to ogs_pfcp_f_seid_t, 8-byte SEID read (and byte-swapped in place) with only presence/NULL checks, no IE length check
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: session-lookup code in the UPF context, F-SEID is a mandatory IE that the report does not mention

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SGW-U Sxa Session Establishment Request: same CP F-SEID cast without IE length check (second copy of the UPF code)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: legacy EPC SGW-U path, not the 5GC UPF the report concerns

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SMF/SGW-C Session Establishment Response: UP F-SEID cast and 8-byte SEID read with no IE length check
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: response path from the CP's own UPF; same pattern also at src/smf/n4-handler.c:1226-1228, src/smf/gsm-sm.c:1038-1040, src/sgwc/sxa-handler.c:325-327, src/sgwc/pfcp-sm.c:283-284

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an ogs_pfcp_parse_user_id counterpart to the existing build function, with length-prefixed IMSI/IMEISV/MSISDN reads checked only for the prefix byte
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Every other build_* in this file has a matching parse_*; the length-prefixed layout mirrors the SDF Filter flow_description case the fix had to patch.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Usage Report handling in the EPC Session Modification Response, parsing Volume Measurement like src/smf/n4-handler.c:1548
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: PFCP allows Usage Reports in Modification Responses; a maintainer would copy the deletion-response loop, giving a third SMF route that sits in a different function from the reported one.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: decode a multi-octet Measurement Information / flag-driven IE into the URR from raw data
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The adjacent code already reads URR IEs straight from octet data; a flag-driven extension would naturally be written in the same unchecked style as the threshold parser.

O9_family: memory safety (native): heap out-of-bounds read in flag-driven TLV field decoding (CWE-125)

O10_build.toolchain: meson + ninja, gcc/clang (meson.build:18-26); depends on libtalloc, libyaml, libmongoc, libgnutls/libgcrypt, libsctp, libmicrohttpd, libnghttp2, libcurl, libidn and bundled freeDiameter
O10_build.project_tests: No unit tests for lib/pfcp/types.c; tests/unit/meson.build:18-31 lists no PFCP test. PFCP behaviour is only covered by the integration suites under tests/ that start NFs and need MongoDB, so hidden tests would best call the lib/pfcp parsers directly as a small unit harness.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add length checks only to ogs_pfcp_parse_dropped_dl_traffic_threshold (or only before its two memcpys, leaving the flags-octet read and the volume/volume-measurement/SDF siblings), relying on the caller's post-hoc len != decoded comparison.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/gtp/v1/types.c and lib/gtp/v2/types.c contain analogous hand-written IE decoders for GTP; not PFCP and not examined.
src/upf/context.c:381 and src/sgwu/context.c:257 byte-swap the SEID in place inside the receive buffer; with a short IE that is a write, not just a read. Noted only.
SMF calls ogs_pfcp_parse_volume_measurement without checking volume_measurement.presence (src/smf/n4-handler.c:1548, src/smf/n4-handler.c:1744); before the fix, data may be NULL for an absent IE.
unverified: j_defence_ineffective=1 is based on the callers' post-parse length comparison (lib/pfcp/handler.c:1680, lib/pfcp/handler.c:1728, src/smf/n4-handler.c:1550), which runs only after the out-of-bounds read. For SDF Filter, the same comparison (lib/pfcp/handler.c:518, lib/pfcp/handler.c:918) appears to stop the oversized flow_description from being used, so that site may only be defence-in-depth. Not proven.
Whether a zero-length VAR_STR IE leaves octet->data NULL or pointing at the next byte depends on ogs_tlv parsing in lib/core/ogs-tlv.c; not read.
Whether the O8 raw-cast reads can go past the end of the pkbuf allocation, rather than into the following IE bytes, depends on where the IE sits in the message; not checked.
repo_mb is unknown; the size was not measured.
O9_dos is false because CWE-125 is an over-read, not resource exhaustion; the practical impact is likely a UPF/SMF crash.
present_in_latest is unknown for all O8 routes because no latest release was given.
